warnings: No tier-1 or tier-2 evidence (AI conversations, interviews, on-site search, win/loss) was available. The strongest evidence in this run is tier-5 public reviews and one forum thread, plus a government secret-shopper study.
Language samples are counts within this small corpus. They are not market frequency and were not used to weight anything.
job-007 rests on a single company-asserted source and is hypothesis_only. job-004 and job-008 rest on weak or company-commissioned evidence and are capped at rotating/sentinel.
Roles are kept separate: care-seeker, practice owner-clinician and practice operations manager are not collapsed. No caregiver role was created because no evidence supports one.
Funnel was not inferred from keywords. Most jobs carry funnel null at the cell level; see prompt_architecture.json for the per-cell rule.

jobs.statement: When I need a new provider in an unfamiliar area or after a plan change, help me get an appointment on the calendar with someone my plan actually covers, near enough to reach, and soon enough to matter.
jobs.struggling_moment: Starting a provider search from zero with three simultaneous constraints (network, location, availability) and no reliable single list that satisfies all three
jobs.desired_progress: A confirmed appointment with a provider who is genuinely covered, without a second round of phone calls
workarounds: Calling the insurer for a list
Asking the previous clinician or local acquaintances
Calling offices one by one to confirm

push.text: Relocation or plan change removes the existing provider relationship

pull.text: Being able to see real open slots and pick one immediately

anxiety.text: The listing may be wrong and the visit may not be covered
A confirmed booking may be cancelled at the last minute

habit.text: Defaulting to the insurer's directory or a phone call

criteria.text: Appointment available within an acceptable window

constraints.text: Cannot verify coverage without a second confirmation

language_samples.text: incredibly easy to book, reschedule, or cancel appointments
got an appointment that quick and with choices

jobs.statement: When a listing says a provider takes my plan, help me confirm that is actually true before I sit in the chair, so I am not handed an out-of-network bill afterwards.
jobs.struggling_moment: The directory and the front desk disagree, and the cost of believing the wrong one lands after the visit
jobs.desired_progress: Confidence that coverage will hold, and a known sequence of checks that produces it
workarounds: Asking for the billing NPI/tax ID and checking it against the plan

pull.text: A filter that claims to show real in-network availability

habit.text: Trusting whatever list the plan publishes

criteria.text: Coverage confirmed by a second, independent check

constraints.text: Verification must happen before the visit; afterwards there is no leverage

language_samples.text: Why would ZocDoc state you are in my network if you are not?

jobs.statement: When every therapist on my plan's list is full, unreachable, or no longer in network, help me actually reach one who will take me, without spending my working day on follow-up calls.
jobs.struggling_moment: Working a list where a third or more of the entries are dead ends, while unable to make repeated daytime calls
jobs.desired_progress: A first session booked within weeks rather than an indefinite search

push.text: 33% of listings inaccurate, non-working or unreturned; over 80% of contacted listings effectively unavailable

pull.text: A list showing who is genuinely accepting new patients

anxiety.text: Repeating the whole exercise and still not being seen

habit.text: Starting again from the insurer's portal

criteria.text: Provider is actually accepting new patients

constraints.text: Limited daytime availability to chase providers

language_samples.text: All therapists are either full or have these weird ass times
Insurance portals just dont have updated contact details
Most of the therapists don't return the call and have full voicemails

jobs.statement: When something needs attention today and my usual provider is booked out, help me find a route to being seen quickly without a referral I do not have and without an unknown price.
jobs.struggling_moment: Acute need collides with weeks-long lead times, referral gatekeeping, and unclear cost
jobs.desired_progress: Seen today or within a day or two, at a knowable price
workarounds: Emergency department as a last resort

push.text: Regular provider has no near-term availability

pull.text: Same-day and no-referral booking options are heavily marketed

anxiety.text: Unknown cost, or coverage refused because a referral was required

habit.text: Calling the practice and accepting the next offered slot

criteria.text: Referral not required, or obtainable fast

constraints.text: Price must be knowable before committing when self-paying

jobs.status_note: Supported for the insured same-day variant via search proxy; the self-pay price-transparency variant (icp-005) is hypothesis_only and was quarantined at QA.

jobs.statement: When my schedule has unfilled capacity, help me decide which channels are worth paying for and what a new patient can cost me before the arithmetic stops working.
jobs.struggling_moment: Deciding whether a per-new-patient fee is a purchase or a leak, without a published rate card and without a settled view of what a new patient is worth
jobs.desired_progress: A defensible blended cost per new patient and a channel mix the owner controls
workarounds: Trialling one marketplace and watching the monthly invoice
Building referrals and owned booking instead

push.text: Per-booking fees that vary unpredictably by specialty and market

pull.text: Bookings arrive from people already ready to schedule

anxiety.text: Renting demand rather than owning it
Fees are not visible until late in sign-up

habit.text: Judging a channel on gross new patients rather than blended cost

criteria.text: Actual unfilled capacity to be filled
Lowest blended cost per new patient across all channels
Whether the channel is owned or rented

constraints.text: Per-new-patient fee cited roughly $35-$110 by specialty and market

language_samples.text: lowest blended cost per new patient
not a one and done solution to filling your practice

jobs.statement: When acquisition charges land for appointments that never happened or for patients we already had, help me get them corrected and stop the monthly total from running away from me.
jobs.struggling_moment: Being billed at booking rather than at attendance, with a bill that changes shape every month
jobs.desired_progress: Disputed charges reversed, and a predictable ceiling on acquisition spend

push.text: Fee is charged whether or not the patient attends

pull.text: Spend caps and pause controls exist

habit.text: Absorbing small disputed charges rather than claiming them

criteria.text: A working dispute path with a defined window
A hard monthly ceiling on spend

constraints.text: Claims window is short (7 days for existing-patient claims; 24-hour good-faith cancellation waiver)

language_samples.text: Should not charge a fee for their mistake
whether or not the client arrives or doesn't

jobs.statement: When inbound scheduling calls exceed what staff can answer, including outside business hours, help me stop losing bookings to hold times and voicemail.
jobs.struggling_moment: Scheduling demand arrives by phone at times and volumes the front office cannot absorb
jobs.desired_progress: Calls resolved into booked appointments without adding staff

push.text: Hold times and unanswered after-hours calls

pull.text: Automated 24/7 call handling that books into the real calendar

jobs.status_note: Derived from a target capability page. This is close to inverting a product feature into demand, which the method forbids. It is admitted only as a quarantined rotating cell and must not enter core without independent or buyer-language evidence.

jobs.statement: When people increasingly consult AI assistants before and instead of contacting a practice, help me understand what that changes about how care is found, chosen and booked this year.
jobs.struggling_moment: Discovery and pre-visit research are moving into assistants and into third-party consumer surfaces, and neither patients nor practices have settled norms for it
jobs.desired_progress: A current, dated understanding of where booking demand now originates and how to respond
workarounds: Reacting to individual incidents in the exam room

push.text: Providers report a rise in AI-informed patients over the past year; 83% report correcting AI-derived misinformation in a visit

pull.text: Booking is being embedded into review and assistant surfaces with real-time in-network availability

anxiety.text: Patients concealing AI use from clinicians (23% have hidden it)

constraints.text: Evidence decays; each derived cell carries a review-by date

jobs.status_note: The only prevalence figures come from a target-commissioned survey (source-010, fielded Feb 2026, published 2026-03-24). They are dated and citable as a market event but are not independent prevalence. source-014 (2021) covers the same theme and is explicitly too old to anchor a B5 cell. Cells derived from job-008 are rotating or sentinel only, never core.
